decisions.what: Database design confirmed: rename the column, drop idx_manual_charge_entries_account_time, replace the vehicle-time index with (tesla_id, charged_on DESC).
decisions.why: No row deleted and no value rewritten, so Down is a true undo. Two indexes become one and it serves all four reads.

decisions.what: UpdateEntry and DeleteEntry keep an account predicate in tier 1, on the renamed column. Tier 2 swaps it for the tesla_id guard. This is the roadmap's D5 and design.md's D4.
decisions.why: Dropping it in tier 1 leaves the write path unauthorized until tier 2. The delete handler proceeds on a lookup miss, so SQL is the only guard, and main auto-deploys.

decisions.what: The artifact worker ran on Opus rather than the default Sonnet.
decisions.why: A DB design gate needs an index plan justified against read patterns plus rejected alternatives. A weak design.md here costs a full re-dispatch and a second user gate.

decisions.what: Kept the test name TestRecentEfficiency_AccountIDScoping_PassedToEveryPort and TestRecalculate_AccountIDScoping_PassedToEveryPort, and only swapped the manual port's assertion from account to vehicle.
decisions.why: tasks.md T6.2 mandates the assertion swap, not a rename. Renaming is wider than the task. Flagged for the reviewer.

decisions.what: Removed the stale design/roadmap decision IDs from Reader.ListEntriesByVehicleBetween's doc comment in charging.go.
decisions.why: The worker rewrote that comment and carried the pointers forward. They name archived docs a later reader cannot open. The opportunistic legacy-cleanup rule covers it.

decisions.what: Accepted the worker's deviation on T5.2: cleanupAccount logs RowsAffected instead of asserting it.
decisions.why: 84 callers; some clean an account that wrote no row, so a non-zero assert fails for the right reason. The checked exec error catches the rename hazard. Flagged to the reviewer.

decisions.what: The leader ran T8 itself instead of dispatching a charging worker.
decisions.why: T8 is guards, greps and hand-off text. A worker would re-read the ~11,900-token base pack to run shell commands.
